description: One-pass review of crate jmap-calendars-server (crate-jmap-calendars-server/). Filed by /review-rusty-crate. Crate version: 0.1.1. Source: 7 modules + lib + 1 helper = 3357 LoC. cargo check / cargo test / cargo clippy all green at start. 36 inline tests pass. Spec basis: draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 (jmap-chat-spec/references/draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26.txt), RFC 8620 (rfc8620.txt). Sister review JMAP-231o covers jmap-calendars-CLIENT — distinct scope.
notes:
Review pass started 2026-05-07. cargo test --workspace passes 36/36 calendars-server tests at baseline. Clippy clean.
Pass complete on 2026-05-07. Filed 25 child findings under JMAP-r3pg: 1 P0 (bug), 7 P1 (3 bug + 4 task), 6 P2, 7 P3, 5 P4 (incl. 2 opinion-tagged). 

Maintainer risk: HIGH — the P0 (.1 calendarHasEvents typo) is a user-visible wire-protocol bug already shipped; clients matching on the spec-correct error name will not recognize the response. The P1 cluster (.2, .3, .5, .7, .8) shows substantial JMAP Calendars semantic gaps: §5.7 /get extra args dropped, §5.11 /query expandRecurrences unimplemented, onDestroyRemoveEvents:true does not actually remove events, onSuccessSetIsDefault unimplemented, sendSchedulingMessages unimplemented. Combined with .4 (account_exists missing on /set) and .6 (client-supplied id accepted on create), this crate is far from spec-complete despite 36 inline tests passing.

Correctness confidence: 65% chance of additional missed bugs. Highest uncertainty: did not verify ResultReference threading from a Calendar/get response into a CalendarEvent/get reference, did not exhaustively re-derive every error code from §10.7, did not check whether the dispatcher's parse_request rejects unknown args (which could shadow the missing §5.7/§5.11 arg parsing if it's strict). Confidence would rise with: a wiremock test driving each method against the spec example JSON in §8.

Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE-BUT-DRIFTING — code compiles clean under -D warnings and passes all inline tests, but the structural patterns differ from the canonical extension-server jmap-mail-server in non-trivial ways (#[non_exhaustive] coverage gap, heavy boilerplate duplication across 4 /set handlers, PLAN.md drift on names/feature flag/module layout). The extra-arg parsing pattern (or lack thereof) means a clean 0.2.0 will require an API break: add CalendarEventGetArgs, CalendarEventQueryArgs, CalendarEventSetArgs structs to thread args through. If that break is going to happen anyway, lock the right shape now and propagate the shape across every extension-server sibling per the cookie-cutter rule in workspace AGENTS.md.

Rust idiom confidence: 75% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: .12 (boilerplate extraction — could go either direction depending on team taste), .19 (std vs tokio Mutex — works correctly today). Did not run cargo-hack feature-powerset (no features in Cargo.toml today, so probably moot — but the 'parse' feature in PLAN.md §11 should land), did not run clippy::pedantic / nursery (might surface 5-10 more nits but unclear if worth filing).

Cross-crate notes: this crate has parallel patterns with jmap-mail-server (the canonical extension-server template, same /set boilerplate) and jmap-calendars-client (JMAP-231o review, distinct findings). Where appropriate, .9 (#[non_exhaustive]), .12 (/set boilerplate), .14 (extract_account_id pattern), .19 (Mutex), .21 (capability URI), .22 (tokio dep), .24 (# Errors docs) all warrant matched-pattern review on jmap-mail-server (and propagation to every extension-server sibling) before any 0.2.0. Reference JMAP-231o.4, JMAP-231o.16, JMAP-231o.34 for the calendars-client siblings of .23, .21, .24.
